overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation as alleged: it declined to review the muting and agenda-order claims and found the notice sufficiently specific. It also reminded the commission to respond to complaints within 14 business days.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair had him muted during the remote-access meeting, preventing him from addressing the commission remotely.
allegations.key_passage: Because the act of muting the complainant during the August 28 meeting, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged he was muted before and after the meeting and that his remote connection was cut abruptly after adjournment.
allegations.key_passage: These allegations concern actions taken by the Commission before and after the meeting and therefore do not implicate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the commission took agenda items out of order, discussing his complaint later than the notice listed it.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not review the allegation that the Commission discussed the Open Meeting Law complaint later in the meeting than suggested by the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice was not specific enough because the meeting discussed his character, which was not listed as a topic.
allegations.key_passage: However, the discussion remained focused on the Open Meeting Law complaints
